title: SketchBuilder: Learning-Augmented Proactive Sketch Construction for Heavy Hitter Detection in Data Streams

problem.claim: Heavy hitter detection in data streams must estimate frequent items accurately and efficiently under constrained memory.

gap.claim: Existing self-adjusting sketches largely overlook persistent global sketch-level collisions, which degrade accuracy and cause costly structural readjustments.

contributions.claim: SketchBuilder is a learning-augmented framework that shifts sketch management from reactive adaptation to proactive construction.
The framework jointly optimizes global item mapping and local memory layout through a Dispatcher and a Constructor using historical sketches to anticipate stream evolution.
SketchBuilder constructs collision-aware, workload-tailored sketches in advance and includes flexible scaling for distribution shifts.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On real-world traces, SketchBuilder achieves an F?-score of 0.99 for top-k detection using 100~KB of memory.
On real-world traces, SketchBuilder achieves 99.70% precision for threshold-t detection using 100~KB of memory.
Compared with SOTA work, the authors report up to 99.81% lower average absolute error and improvements in both accuracy and efficiency.

narrative_sequence.summary: Heavy hitter detection is an important data-stream processing problem.
Self-adjusting sketches react to skewed streams by repeatedly modifying local memory structures.
Persistent global collisions among heavy hitters reduce accuracy and increase structural adjustment overhead.
SketchBuilder proactively constructs sketches by coordinating global mapping refinement with predicted local memory allocation.
Experiments on real-world traces report strong detection and precision metrics under a 100~KB memory budget and lower average absolute error than SOTA work.
